transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-08-04, Start: 15:00 UTC, Duration: 48m. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Camila (Redwood SE), Liam (GreenPort ML), Priya (GreenPort Platform), Daniel (GreenPort Security)

Summary: Brief intake to understand GreenPort's inference footprint, isolation/tenancy requirements, burst patterns for clinical-read workloads, and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agreed to pilot with burst window and perf run.

Topics: scope, reserved GPU sizing, hot-pool/prewarm, VPC/on-prem path, KMS/keys, SOC2/ISO evidence, pricing and SLA expectations, fallback models and canary rollouts.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run 45 ish minutes, quick intros then jump into your current infra and what you're trying to protect.
[00:18] Liam: yeah thanks, i'm liam, we run inference for a mix of clinical summarization and triage, latency sensitive at p50 but p95 matters for user experience, ok—sorry—p95 matters for provider workflows.
[00:34] Priya: priya here; platform runs on k8s in a single cloud region today, we use autoscaling for the web tier but model inference is… we're currently pushing to managed endpoints but costs are spiking.
[00:51] Daniel: daniel, i'm security, main things for us: audit logs, key management, data residency and SOC2 evidence. we also have to show separation between test and prod.
[01:06] Maya: great, high level, we offer three modes — hosted api for quick onboarding, dedicated reserved GPUs for predictable throughput and isolation, and private (VPC or on-prem) for strict controls. today i'd like to understand your burst profile, expected steady qps and critical SLAs.
[01:28] Liam: steady is like 20 rps on average, but we have nightly batch jobs and occasional surges during morning rounds—peak can be 140 rps for short windows, maybe 3–8 minutes, sometimes up to 20 minutes.
[01:46] Jordan: ok, and how many tokens per request on average?
[01:50] Liam: average prompt + response is around 900 tokens, sometimes 2k for long summarizations.
[02:05] Camila: that helps size GPU memory/kv cache. for bursts of 140 rps at 900 tokens we'd probably suggest dedicated hot-pool prewarmed into reserved nodes plus dynamic burst to shared capacity, is that accurate?
[02:22] Priya: what does "shared capacity" mean for data isolation? we can't have PHI flowing through multi-tenant pools without encryption and contractual guarantees.
[02:33] Maya: totally—shared capacity can be used for overflow but for PHI we recommend either dedicated reserved nodes or private VPC where data never leaves your control plane. we can encrypt in transit and at rest; we also integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
[02:50] Daniel: do you support bringing your own KMS? we use an HSM-backed KMS and need key access controls and rotation proof.
[02:58] Camila: yes, BYOK is supported for private and dedicated; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integration and we can show key rotation logs.
[03:12] Liam: timeline—we want a pilot in september, production by q4 if things look good. cost is a gating factor.
[03:21] Maya: got it. cost vs latency tradeoff question: you can run smaller quantized model variants to save on GPU hours but p95 will change. are you flexible on model fidelity?
[03:34] Liam: for triage maybe yes, but clinical summarization needs high fidelity. we may tier models: cheaper for non-critical, larger for final summaries.
[03:45] Jordan: technical follow-up: do you need pinning of model versions across nodes for canary rollouts?
[03:51] Priya: yes, we require deterministic rollouts and ability to rollback quickly if quality regresses. also per-team RBAC so dev vs prod can't access the same pool.
[04:06] Maya: we have route-level policies, canary/A-B and auto-fallback to a smaller model or hosted variant on overload. RBAC and SAML SSO integrations are supported.
[04:18] Daniel: retention policies—logs need to be kept 1 year and immutable exports for audits. can you deliver audit exports?
[04:27] Camila: we can provide audit logs and a compliance pack, plus long-term log export to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[04:36] Liam: curious about prewarm — do you keep a hot-pool ready? what's the cost?
[04:42] Jordan: we offer a warm/hot pool model. hot pool is reserved GPU capacity that stays preloaded with your model weights and kv cache so cold-start latency is minimal. cost is a function of reserved node hours plus a small snapshot fee; we'll share a sample cost model in the deck.
[04:58] Priya: ok can you handle on-prem? we may want private deployment in our VPC initially and later move to dedicated in Redwood cloud.
[05:06] Camila: yes, private deployment is possible; there's a customer-managed control plane option. networking requirements include egress rules for health checks and a connection to Redwood control plane for telemetry if you choose managed mode.
[05:24] Liam: fallback behavior—if my dedicated pool is saturated, do you throttle or route to hosted slower model? we need predictable degradation, not bursts causing errors.
[05:34] Maya: by policy we can route overflow to a lower-cost hosted variant, or reject once a hard quota is hit. recommended is a staged fallback: first scale within reserved pool, then warm-burst to partner capacity, then fallback to hosted small model, with circuit-breaker thresholds.
[05:54] Priya: who owns the failover routing, us or you? we need the ability to turn it off during sensitive windows.
[06:02] Jordan: failover policy is customer-configurable; Redwood defaults can be applied but you can set blackout windows.
[06:10] Daniel: security question—do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001? we need the reports or at least an attestation.
[06:18] Maya: yes SOC2 type II and ISO evidence available; we'll send the security pack and a pointer to our compliance portal.
[06:26] Liam: one more on metrics—token-level cost breakdown by route and by token type? we need to charge back to internal teams.
[06:35] Camila: console has route-level cost and latency breakdown, you can also export per-token accounting for internal chargeback.
[06:45] Priya: networking: can you do private peering or do we have to use a VPN? latency is sensitive.
[06:53] Jordan: we support VPC peering and private link equivalents depending on cloud. we'll outline options in the architecture note.
[07:03] Liam: examples of similar customers?
[07:07] Maya: we have a couple of healthcare customers on dedicated with hybrid private setups. we'll anonymize case studies and share latency/cost figures.
[07:18] Daniel: how do you handle data residency for europe? we have teams in EU.
[07:23] Camila: you can pin workloads to region and we support private deployment into EU regions.
[07:30] Priya: do you support quantization for M60-ish models or specific hardware?
[07:36] Jordan: yes we recommend quantized variants for cost savings; kernel selection and perf will vary by GPU family. we'll include recommendations based on your token distribution.
[07:50] Liam: action items recap?
[07:53] Maya: sure — i'll send pricing + hot-pool model, jordan will run perf test on hosted baseline, camila will send VPC/onprem checklist, liam to share sample prompts.
[08:05] Priya: can you include an example SLA for p99/p95 latency? and SLOs for model quality?
[08:12] Maya: yes we'll include a sample SLA and propose SLO targets based on the perf run.
[08:18] Liam: final ask — can we get a 24 hour benchmark window with a hosted instance using a subset of our prompts?
[08:24] Jordan: yes we'll set that up; will need sample data and a safe scrubbed subset for PII.
[08:32] Daniel: security will need the security pack and a short questionnaire before we sign off for pilot.
[08:38] Maya: we'll share the security questionnaire and SOC2 docs.

Recap (end): agreed pilot in September, next steps listed in action items. GreenPort to confirm pilot timeline by 2026-08-10.

References mentioned: pricing deck link (to be provided), security pack (link), VPC onboarding checklist (link).

Notes about transcript quality: minor mis-hears on acronyms, some crosstalk at 03:00–03:30.

Meeting ended 15:48 UTC.
